From Wiktionary, the free dictionary
See also: biscottò

English

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Italian biscotto. Doublet of biscuit.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Received Pronunciation) IPA(key): /bɪˈskɒtəʊ/
  • Audio (Southern England):(file)
  • (General American) IPA(key): /bɪˈskɑtoʊ/
  • Rhymes: -ɒtəʊ

Noun

[edit]

biscotto (plural biscotti)

  1. Alternative form of biscotti.

French

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Italian biscotto (“cookie, biscuit”) (in a figurative sense). Doublet of biscuit and biscotte.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /bis.kɔ.to/
  • Rhymes: -o

Noun

[edit]

biscotto m (uncountable)

  1. (sports) tactical play between two people (or two teams) aimed to wrong or evict a third person (or a third team)

Italian

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /bisˈkɔt.to/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Rhymes: -ɔtto
  • Hyphenation: bi‧scòt‧to

Etymology 1

[edit]

Inherited from Early Medieval Latin biscoctus. Synchronicallty bis- (“twice”) +‎ cotto (“baked, cooked”). Doublet of biscuit.

Noun

[edit]

biscotto m (plural biscotti)

  1. biscuit, cookie
  2. (sports slang, uncountable) match fixing, tactical play between two teams aimed to wrong or evict a third team
    Synonym: combine
Derived terms
[edit]
  • biscottaio
  • biscottare
  • biscottato
  • biscottello
  • biscotteria
  • biscottiera
  • biscottificio
  • biscottino
Descendants
[edit]
  • → Byzantine Greek: μπισκόττιν (mpiskóttin)
    • Greek: μπισκότο (biskóto)
  • → English: biscotti, biscotto
  • → French: biscotte; biscotto
  • → German: Biskotte; → Zwieback (calque) (see there for further descendants)
  • → Hijazi Arabic: بِسْكوت (biskōt)
  • → Spanish: biscotte

Etymology 2

[edit]

See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form.

Verb

[edit]

biscotto

  1. first-person singular present indicative of biscottare
